{\int }_{0}^{8}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{0}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{2}^{8}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{2}}.
$$

The 1st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [0,2].$ The corresponding region is a right triangle, so we find the area using the formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2\cdot 2 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we have 

$$

$$

$$

$$

Example: 
                    Finding Points That Satisfy the Mean Value Theorem for Integrals
canonical_examples.problem: Find the values of $c$ that satisfy the mean value theorem for integrals for  $f(x) = x^2-2x+2$ on the interval $[0,3].$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Applying the mean value theorem for integrals, we have

$$
\eqalign{
       f(c) (b-a)  & =  \int_a^b f(x) \, \textrm dx \[5pt]
              f(c)    & = \dfrac {1}{b-a} \int_a^b f(x) \, \textrm dx \[5pt]
    & = \dfrac {1}{3-0} \int_0^3  (x^2-2x+2) \, \textrm dx \[5pt]
     & =  \left . \dfrac {1}{3} \cdot  \left[\dfrac{x^3}{3} -x^2 +2x\right] \right|_0^3 \[5pt]
    & =   \dfrac {1}{3} \cdot \left[ \left(\dfrac{3^3}{3} -3^2 +2\cdot3\right) -  \left(\dfrac{0^3}{3} -0^2 +2\cdot0\right)\right] \[5pt]
    & =  \dfrac {1}{3}\cdot6 \[5pt]
    &  = 2.
}
$$

    

Now, we use the expression for $f(x)$ to solve for the value of $c\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(c) & =2 \\ {c}^{2}-2c+2 & =2 \\ c(c-2) & =0 \\ c & =0,2.\end{aligned}
$$

Example: 
                    Finding the Average Value of a Function Over a Given Interval
canonical_examples.problem: Find the average value of the function $f(x) = x - 2$ on the interval $[-2, 4].$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Applying the average value formula, we find that the average value of the function is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{\text{avg}} & =\frac{1}{b-a}\,{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{4-(-2)}{\int }_{-2}^{4}x-2\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{6}(\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}-2x){|}_{-2}^{4} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}[(\frac{{4}^{2}}{2}-2(4))-(\frac{(-2)^{2}}{2}-2(-2))] \\  & =\frac{1}{6}[(8-8)-(2+4)] \\  & =\frac{1}{6}(0-6) \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

                    Finding an Interval Given the Average Value of a Function
canonical_examples.problem: Find $c$ such that the average value of $g(x) = 3 x$ on the interval $[0,c]$ is equal to $3.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
To solve for $c,$ we apply the average value formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{\text{avg}} & =\frac{1}{b-a}\,{\int }_{a}^{b}g(x)\,\text{d}x \\ 3 & =\frac{1}{c-0}\,{\int }_{0}^{c}3x\,\text{d}x \\ 3 & =\frac{1}{c}(\frac{3{x}^{2}}{2}){|}_{0}^{c} \\ 3 & =\frac{1}{c}(\frac{3{c}^{2}}{2}-0) \\ 3 & =\frac{3c}{2} \\ c & =2\end{aligned}
$$

tutorials.problem:
The region $\textrm{R},$ shown below, is the area under the graph of $f(x) = 2x+1$ over the interval $[1,3].$ What is the height of the rectangle defined over the same interval that has the same area as $\textrm{R}?$ 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14153257/assets/01597200b1f0e147fa8c53b6301d0c8e37208b5a6cce64cf0d9859d1220d8385.png)

 

Using the formula for the area of a trapezoid, we have that

$$
\eqalign{
\textrm{Area}\,(\textrm{R}) = \dfrac{1}{2}(3+7)(3-1)= 10.}
$$

For the rectangle to have the same area, we must have 

$$
\begin{aligned}10 & =f(c)(3-1) \\ f(c) & =5 \\ 2c+1 & =5 \\ c & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

We can summarize what we've just done by saying that

$$
\int_1^3 (2x +1)\, \textrm d x= f(2) \cdot (3-1).
$$

This is an example of the **mean value theorem for integrals**, which states:

*If $f(x)$ is a continuous function on the closed interval $[a, b]$, then there exists a number $c$ in that interval such that*

$$
\int_a^b f(x)\, \textrm d x = f(c) \cdot (b-a).
$$
